rules.generalizes_with_caveats: Same direction but magnitude ratio < 50%, or caveat applies.
rules.does_not_generalize: Opposite directions or one dataset null when other is strong.
rules.asvspoof_specific: Only meaningful on ASVspoof (labeled attack systems).

KL range widening (robust > baseline).notes: ASVspoof has 3.2x range vs MLAAD 1.6x — same direction but ASVspoof effect is ~2.5x larger. Widening is present on both but weaker for MLAAD.

Top-2 ablation effect in robust checkpoi.notes: Both datasets: ablation ΔEER well above random ctrl. Mag ratio ≈ 0.55 (ASVspoof gap=0.040, MLAAD gap=0.072).

Top-2 ablation effect in baseline checkp.notes: ASVspoof: robust_goat's heads {h0,h4} don't transfer to goat (ΔEER=0, 57th pct). MLAAD: robust_goat's heads {h2,h4} fully transfer to goat (ΔEER=+0.090, 100th pct). Head identity is checkpoint-invariant in MLAAD but not in ASVspoof.

Null distribution percentile (cross-chec.notes: Both tests use the same paradigm: apply robust's target heads to the goat and compare to 14-pair exhaustive null. ASVspoof result is chance-level (57%); MLAAD is at maximum (100%). This reinforces claim 3: head identity only cross-checkpoint stable in MLAAD.

Entropy collapse (robust_goat top heads.notes: Both: robustness training sharpens top heads (lower entropy). Effect ~3x smaller in MLAAD (Δ≈−0.15) than ASVspoof (Δ≈−0.50). Same direction across all systems.

Per-class F1 cascade (attack-system clas.notes: ASVspoof has 6 labeled attack systems enabling per-class F1. MLAAD's 63 systems are too numerous for stable per-class estimates with the available sample sizes.

GAT-localized: pre_gat features byte-ide.notes: Strongest claim: encoder weights are frozen; all robustness-training changes are localized to GAT+BiLSTM. Confirmed byte-identically on both datasets.

Linear probe ordering: post_wavlm vs pre.mlaad_value: post_wavlm=0.1522  pre_gat=0.3976  post_gat_g=0.4030  order: post_wavlm << pre_gat ≈ post_gat
Linear probe ordering: post_wavlm vs pre.notes: Opposite orderings. ASVspoof: phoneme pooling (pre_gat) IMPROVES linear separability over raw WavLM — encoder adds discriminative structure. MLAAD: phoneme pooling DRAMATICALLY degrades separability (EER 0.15→0.40). Both still confirm GAT-localized since the change between checkpoints is zero at pre_gat. This may reflect the difference in dataset difficulty: ASVspoof has 6 known attack systems; MLAAD has 63 heterogeneous TTS/VC systems spanning 2025 models.

Cross-language generalization gap.mlaad_value: post_wavlm gap=+0.0431  pre_gat gap=+0.0306  post_gat gap=+0.0615  ablating h2+h4 reduces robust gap by 0.216
Cross-language generalization gap.notes: MLAAD provides a direct cross-language test. Post-GAT features degrade most across languages (gap=+0.070 vs +0.043 at post_wavlm). Ablating h2+h4 on robust_goat reduces the in/out-of-distribution gap by 0.217, identifying these heads as language-overfitting components.

Language-invariant attention routing (cr.mlaad_value: h2: cos_sim=0.9528  h4: cos_sim=0.9481 (10 shared attack systems, in-dist vs cross-lang)
Language-invariant attention routing (cr.notes: Despite ablating these heads dramatically improving cross-language EER, the attention PATTERNS themselves are stable (cos_sim≈0.95). Contradiction: heads encode language-harmful features at the routing level but their attention matrices look similar across languages. Suggests downstream representation use (BiLSTM) is the language-sensitive component, not the attention selection itself.
